questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Language, host university

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The stay was great. Wonderful town, great people and the University was excellent. I wish however that it would have been less bureaucratically difficult. Information is complicated to get to and sparse and I wonder why. I think it could be streamlined a bit. The only way I figured out how to do, was through friends that had previously been on exchange and during my stay I was contacted by students going next semester because they had difficulty finding it out as well.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Upon arrival information was all right. The difficult thing was the entire application process, mobility online, pre-approval and so on.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Im very sorry to point it out, but very little assistance was available. For Studentenwerk everything was perfect and easy to find out, but the coordination with the hospital and the different departments was very sparse. Most of the time the departments didn't know I was coming, what i should do (they thought I was a PJ) which I wasn't. Another complaint is that I never received a uniform card for the hospital. I spend every day there and was treated as a PJ (whom uniform cards are given to), but was never able to get a uniform myself. I tried to talk to the hospital, but they refused. I must admit I think its to bad that when you spend every day for three months in the hospital you can't get a card to the uniforms.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: As I have commented on previously, this wasn't so great. I don't know whether it is because I only was at the hospital in a clinical rotation, but I was never given contact information to the department of which I should stay. When I asked about information about location I was given a location that hasn't been used in 6 years. I also got the impression that I had to push for things to be done and write multiple mails to the host university to ensure that things were being done.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Studentenwerk. Small study apartments.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: No meal plans. Small kitchen shared with roomie. Worked fine.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I found it great. It was a bit old and roughed up, but overall it was very affordable and work perfectly. I would definitely recommend.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Honestly this was one of the most stressing and complicated processes I have ever dealt with. No information, different protocols for host and home university. Things like the host university said that I could not continue before I did a certain thing and the home university said that I could not continue before I did the opposite thing. As I said previously, the only way to figure this out is by writing to other students who have previously been on exchange and they continue to do this. I have a very hard time understanding why this process can be so complicated when it is done every year, Perhaps it would be possible to create a step by step guide that explains what you should do next.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Upon arrival the Studentenwerk helps with first hand advice of how to get settled in. That was great. The whole deal with getting departments in the hospital was as previously described tedious and complicated. First my learning agreement and the dates of the stay was approved and then some time after I was told that I would have to come back in february, which would be after I finished the given semester, and then I had to basically myself figure out another department that could take me the one week which I need. It was just extremely complicated.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The secretary at the medical faculty of Heidelberg, but I must admit that the person concerned mostly didn't reply before I wrote two or three mails.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Complicated but it worked out.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know write multiple mails at first so you get a response. Start early because it will take a while.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was satisfied with some of the departments which were truly excellent, but I must say a general thing was that they did not know I was coming, what I was supposed to do and so on. I found this a bit sad as I during my surgical stay only came to the operating theater 5 times during 5 weeks... I think maybe a problem was that the amount of PJ's (medical students undergoing their own clinical rotation in Heidelberg) where way to many. In the surgical department we were, at one point, 7 students in one bed ward, thats far to many and it hinderes the learning opportunities.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only did clinical stay.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I only did clinical courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: I only did clinical stay: 2 weeks anesthesiology, 5 weeks medical and 5 weeks surgical

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: anesthesiology at Heidelberg Oropädische Klinik was excellent. Mediccal stay in the Notfallsambulanz was great and kinderchirurgie.

Additional comments:
questions.answer: Great sporting facilities and language courses.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: all kinds of sports and bar crawls and parties and so on.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: do some sports. Healthy and great way to socialize.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go the surrounding cities (Mannheim, Strasburg) and so on

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: No problem that I found very easy. You have to remember to say Mr. and Ms. and "Sie"

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take a language course.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Formality.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Many things! I think mostly that it really is the hard of Europe and you meet so many different people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Find someone who has been on exchange before so that they can help you with the complicated application and dont get to sad about it. It sucks but its worth it.
Learn the language and thus the heart of the culture
Do some activities with others.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: A more streamlined guide to application and registration.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning more german, understanding a different country's healthcare system and meeting new freinds.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The bureaucracy. We must fix this guys it was so terribly complciated.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Please ask if medical students that does clinical stays at Heidelberg University Hospital can have a uniform card.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
